sample_unit: clinical questions derived from cervical spine guidelines

links.outcome: Citation validity of sources in generative AI outputs (fully correct, partially or fully hallucinated)
links.effect: OE 999 citations with 100% accuracy; only 184/393 (46.8%) ChatGPT citations accurate (p<.001); 88 (22.4%) ChatGPT citations partially hallucinated.
links.quote: OE generated 999 citations with 100% accuracy, whereas only 184/393 (46.8%) ChatGPT citations met accuracy criteria (p<.001).

links.outcome: Guideline alignment and hallucination rate of evidence-grounded OE versus general ChatGPT
links.effect: OE, prioritizing verified peer-reviewed literature, had higher guideline alignment (4.6±0.8 vs 4.1±0.7; p=.03) and 100% citation accuracy vs 46.8% for ChatGPT.
links.quote: OE demonstrated higher guideline alignment than ChatGPT (4.6±0.8 vs 4.1±0.7; p=.03), with almost perfect interrater agreement (weighted Cohen's κ = 0.88; 95% CI, 0.80-0.97).

unlisted_practices: Prompt-engineering effects on citation validity; reformatting OE output through ChatGPT reduced accuracy (cross-model contamination)

screen.reason: The study empirically compares clinical guideline queries across OpenEvidence and ChatGPT-4o, evaluating hallucination rates and guideline alignment, and specifically tests prompt engineering variations/reformatting effects on citation validity.
